details.expected: Safety advice · Check a timed gap. For the three-second following-distance guideline, select a fixed roadside point, such as a pole or sign. When the rear of the vehicle ahead passes it, start counting at a steady seconds pace. Stop when the front of your car reaches the same point. Arriving before three seconds indicates a short gap against that guideline: ease back smoothly and check again. Three seconds is a guideline, not a statutory fixed interval or a guarantee; poor grip, visibility or other hazards require more space and an appropriate speed. Keep observing the road while counting. NSW Government: fixed-point following-gap method

details.expected: Physical explanation · Twice the speed. With the same effective grip and braking deceleration on the same gradient, braking distance is approximately proportional to speed squared: 2 × speed → 4 × braking distance. In a constant-deceleration model, distance = speed² ÷ (2 × deceleration), with speed in metres per second. Doubling speed multiplies the numerator by four. Real conditions and brake response can change; this is a comparison under stated assumptions. Trafikverket: VGU braking-distance equation

Arriving before three seconds indicates a short gap against that guideline: ease back smoothly and check again. Three seconds is a guideline, not a statutory fixed interval or a guarantee; poor grip, visibility or other hazards require more space and an appropriate speed. A timed gap therefore represents more metres at higher speed, without requiring you to estimate metres by eye.
